title: Taboos in Chinese Drinking Culture
synopsis: If you are about to have a drink with someone in China, make sure to first learn these Chinese drinking culture taboos.

fullText.simplified:
酒桌上的禁忌

    中国人的生意十有八九是在酒桌上谈成的。因为在酒桌上大家可以不用像在正式场合时那么拘谨。而且酒精可以起到让人放松戒备心理，麻痹人的警惕性的作用，会更容易促成双方合作的达成。很多时候如果让合作方在酒桌上喝得满意了，合同往往也就签下来了。但酒桌上有一些禁忌我们是必须了解的。
    首先，酒桌上的座位次序很重要。一般的酒桌都是圆桌，对着房间大门的位置是主位。主位上会放一块红色的方巾，用以区别于其他的位置。主位一般是主陪，也就是买单的人坐的位置。主位右边的是主宾，也就是酒桌上最尊贵的客人坐的位置。所以酒桌上的位置是不可以随便乱坐的。
    其次，敬酒的时候也有很多门道。敬酒人的酒杯一定要比对方的酒杯口低。敬酒的时候，杯子里的酒一定得倒满。忌讳用半杯酒敬酒，否则会显得敬酒人极其不礼貌。敬酒时一定要按照职务大小或者地位的尊贵依次敬酒。还有一点要记住，那就是不可以只用一杯酒敬多个人，敬一个人就得喝一杯酒。
    在中国，酒场如战场，酒桌上的表现至关重要。所以，一定不能触犯禁忌，否则有可能会给对方留下极差的印象，甚至会影响合作的达成。
fullText.traditional:
酒桌上的禁忌

    中國人的生意十有八九是在酒桌上談成的。因為在酒桌上大家可以不用像在正式場合時那麼拘謹。而且酒精可以起到讓人放鬆戒備心理，麻痺人的警惕性的作用，會更容易促成雙方合作的達成。很多時候如果讓合作方在酒桌上喝得滿意了，合同往往也就簽下來了。但酒桌上有一些禁忌我們是必須了解的。
    首先，酒桌上的座位次序很重要。一般的酒桌都是圓桌，對著房間大門的位置是主位。主位上會放一塊紅色的方巾，用以區別於其他的位置。主位一般是主陪，也就是買單的人坐的位置。主位右邊的是主賓，也就是酒桌上最尊貴的客人坐的位置。所以酒桌上的位置是不可以隨便亂坐的。
    其次，敬酒的時候也有很多門道。敬酒人的酒杯一定要比對方的酒杯口低。敬酒的時候，杯子裡的酒一定得倒滿。忌諱用半杯酒敬酒，否則會顯得敬酒人極其不禮貌。敬酒時一定要按照職務大小或者地位的尊貴依次敬酒。還有一點要記住，那就是不可以只用一杯酒敬多個人，敬一個人就得喝一杯酒。
    在中國，酒場如戰場，酒桌上的表現至關重要。所以，一定不能觸犯禁忌，否則有可能會給對方留下極差的印象，甚至會影響合作的達成。

sentences.traditional: 因為在酒桌上大家可以不用像在正式場合時那麼拘謹。
sentences.pinyin: yīn wèi zài jiǔ zhuō shang dà jiā kě yǐ bú yòng xiàng zài zhèng shì chǎng hé shí nà me jū jǐn
sentences.english: For Chinese people, around 80 to 90 percent of business deals are reached while drinking.

sentences.simplified: 而且酒精可以起到让人放松戒备心理，麻痹人的警惕性的作用，
sentences.traditional: 而且酒精可以起到讓人放鬆戒備心理，麻痺人的警惕性的作用，
sentences.pinyin: ér qiě jiǔ jīng kě yǐ qǐ dào ràng rén fàng sōng jiè bèi xīn lǐ má bì rén de jǐng tì xìng de zuò yòng
sentences.english: This is because while drinking, people do not need to be as reserved as they are in formal occasions.

sentences.simplified: 会更容易促成双方合作的达成。
sentences.traditional: 會更容易促成雙方合作的達成。
sentences.pinyin: huì gèng róng yì cù chéng shuāng fāng hé zuò de dá chéng
sentences.english: Additionally, alcohol can help people let their guard down and slacken their vigilance.

sentences.simplified: 很多时候如果让合作方在酒桌上喝得满意了，合同往往也就签下来了。
sentences.traditional: 很多時候如果讓合作方在酒桌上喝得滿意了，合同往往也就簽下來了。
sentences.pinyin: hěn duō shí hou rú guǒ ràng hé zuò fāng zài jiǔ zhuō shang hē de mǎn yì le hé tong wǎng wǎng yě jiù qiān xià lai le
sentences.english: This makes it easier for the two parties to agree collaboration.

sentences.simplified: 但酒桌上有一些禁忌我们是必须了解的。
sentences.traditional: 但酒桌上有一些禁忌我們是必須了解的。
sentences.pinyin: dàn jiǔ zhuō shang yǒu yì xiē jìn jì wǒ men shì bì xū liǎo jiě de
sentences.english: Oftentimes, if the business partner is satisfied by the drinking, the contract will usually get signed as well.
However, there are some drinking taboos that we must understand.

sentences.simplified: 首先，酒桌上的座位次序很重要。
sentences.traditional: 首先，酒桌上的座位次序很重要。
sentences.pinyin: shǒu xiān jiǔ zhuō shang de zuò wèi cì xù hěn zhòng yào

sentences.simplified: 一般的酒桌都是圆桌，对着房间大门的位置是主位。
sentences.traditional: 一般的酒桌都是圓桌，對著房間大門的位置是主位。
sentences.pinyin: yì bān de jiǔ zhuō dōu shì yuán zhuō duì zhe fáng jiān dà mén de wèi zhi shì zhǔ wèi
sentences.english: First, the order in which people sit at the table is very important.

sentences.simplified: 主位上会放一块红色的方巾，用以区别于其他的位置。
sentences.traditional: 主位上會放一塊紅色的方巾，用以區別於其他的位置。
sentences.pinyin: zhǔ wèi shang huì fàng yí kuài hóng sè de fāng jīn yòng yǐ qū bié yú qí tā de wèi zhi
sentences.english: Most tables at which the drinking happens are round tables, and the seat opposite of the door is the host’s seat.

sentences.simplified: 主位一般是主陪，
sentences.traditional: 主位一般是主陪，
sentences.pinyin: zhǔ wèi yì bān shì zhǔ péi
sentences.english: At the host’s seat there will be a square of red fabric, used to differentiate this seat from the others.

sentences.simplified: 也就是买单的人坐的位置。
sentences.traditional: 也就是買單的人坐的位置。
sentences.pinyin: yě jiù shì mǎi dān de rén zuò de wèi zhi
sentences.english: Typically, the host’s seat is for the most important person of the host party, ..

sentences.simplified: 主位右边的是主宾，也就是酒桌上最尊贵的客人坐的位置。
sentences.traditional: 主位右邊的是主賓，也就是酒桌上最尊貴的客人坐的位置。
sentences.pinyin: zhǔ wèi yòu bian de shì zhǔ bīn yě jiù shì jiǔ zhuō shang zuì zūn guì de kè rén zuò de wèi zhi
sentences.english: .. that is the seat of the person who pays the bill.

sentences.simplified: 所以酒桌上的位置是不可以随便乱坐的。
sentences.traditional: 所以酒桌上的位置是不可以隨便亂坐的。
sentences.pinyin: suǒ yǐ jiǔ zhuō shang de wèi zhi shì bù kě yǐ suí biàn luàn zuò de
sentences.english: To the right of the host’s seat is the seat of the guest of honor, that is, the seat for the most important guest.
So, one cannot just simply sit anywhere at the drinking table.

sentences.simplified: 其次，敬酒的时候也有很多门道。
sentences.traditional: 其次，敬酒的時候也有很多門道。
sentences.pinyin: qí cì jìng jiǔ de shí hou yě yǒu hěn duō mén dao

sentences.simplified: 敬酒人的酒杯一定要比对方的酒杯口低。
sentences.traditional: 敬酒人的酒杯一定要比對方的酒杯口低。
sentences.pinyin: jìng jiǔ rén de jiǔ bēi yí dìng yào bǐ duì fāng de jiǔ bēi kǒu dī
sentences.english: Next, there are also many intricacies when it comes to giving toasts.

sentences.simplified: 敬酒的时候，杯子里的酒一定得倒满。
sentences.traditional: 敬酒的時候，杯子裡的酒一定得倒滿。

sentences.english: The person giving the toast must have their glass lower than that of the other person.

sentences.simplified: 否则会显得敬酒人极其不礼貌。

sentences.pinyin: fǒu zé huì xiǎn de jìng jiǔ rén jí qí bù lǐ mào
sentences.english: Giving a toast with only half a glass must be avoided, ..

sentences.simplified: 敬酒时一定要按照职务大小或者地位的尊贵依次敬酒。
sentences.traditional: 敬酒時一定要按照職務大小或者地位的尊貴依次敬酒。

sentences.pinyin: suǒ yǐ yí dìng bù néng chù fàn jìn jì
sentences.english: In China, drinking sessions are like battles. One’s performance at the drinking table is extremely important.

sentences.simplified: 否则有可能会给对方留下极差的印象，甚至会影响合作的达成。
sentences.traditional: 否則有可能會給對方留下極差的印象，甚至會影響合作的達成。

sentences.english: Thus, it is imperative to avoid taboos.
Otherwise, one may leave a very bad impression on the other party, which may even affect agreement on collaboration.

raw.synopsis: If you are about to have a drink with someone in China, make sure to first learn these Chinese drinking culture taboos.
sentence_translations: Taboos in Chinese Drinking Culture
For Chinese people, around 80 to 90 percent of business deals are reached while drinking.
This is because while drinking, people do not need to be as reserved as they are in formal occasions.
Additionally, alcohol can help people let their guard down and slacken their vigilance.
This makes it easier for the two parties to agree collaboration.
Oftentimes, if the business partner is satisfied by the drinking, the contract will usually get signed as well.
However, there are some drinking taboos that we must understand.
First, the order in which people sit at the table is very important.
Most tables at which the drinking happens are round tables, and the seat opposite of the door is the host’s seat.
At the host’s seat there will be a square of red fabric, used to differentiate this seat from the others.
Typically, the host’s seat is for the most important person of the host party, ..
.. that is the seat of the person who pays the bill.
To the right of the host’s seat is the seat of the guest of honor, that is, the seat for the most important guest.
So, one cannot just simply sit anywhere at the drinking table.
Next, there are also many intricacies when it comes to giving toasts.
The person giving the toast must have their glass lower than that of the other person.
When giving the toast, the glass must be full.
Giving a toast with only half a glass must be avoided, ..
.. otherwise the person giving the toast will appear extremely impolite.
When giving a toast, one must toast guests in order of their seniority or status.
Another thing to remember is that one cannot use the same glass of liquor to toast multiple people.
After toasting someone, one must drink the glass of liquor.
In China, drinking sessions are like battles. One’s performance at the drinking table is extremely important.
Thus, it is imperative to avoid taboos.
Otherwise, one may leave a very bad impression on the other party, which may even affect agreement on collaboration.
